messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran a quick sim on hosted token burn vs committed GPUs. Looks like our current model for reserved capacity (flat % of peak) underestimates tail demand for bursty embedding traffic.

ashley: can you share numbers?

maria: sure — short summary: over last 30d peak q99 tokens/sec per region -> eu-west ~42k, us-central ~88k. Our commit plan buys ~65% of q99 capacity across regions. Using current batching this is ok avg, but when long-sequence LLM jobs spike, latency SLOs hit.

devon: is this the same effect as the KV cache cold-warm transitions?

maria: related. Two drivers: long sequences (larger per-request token cost) and embedding bursts from large customers. KV cache helps prefix reuse but embeddings usually miss cache.

liam: ok — proposal?

maria: proposing a tokenized safety margin: allocate reserved GPUs by converting committed capacity to an expected token throughput using per-GPU token/sec profiles, then apply a stochastic cushion (P95 of historical multiplier). That gives us a dynamic commit target instead of flat % of peak.

ashley: interesting. how do we compute per-GPU token/sec?

maria: we have perf profiles per instance type in metrics-db. e.g., p4d-8: ~1.2M tokens/sec for plain gen at seq=512, but drops with longer seq. We'll weight by observed seq distribution and request mix.

devon: math sounds good. any quick numbers from the sim?

maria: from the sim (30d, eu-west): baseline commit -> 12 GPUs, tokenized model -> 16 GPUs for P95 cushion. Cost delta ~+13% committed spend but reduces fallback to on-demand by ~70% during tails.

liam: and impact on hosted billing? are we overcommitting unused capacity most of the time?

maria: there's some idle time — maybe 20% of reserved capacity unused at median. But on-demand fallbacks cost us much more during spikes (both in $ and SLO penalties). Tokenized model optimizes across that tradeoff.

ashley: what about spot/credits and billing SKU mapping? last month finance flagged some unexpected credits not applied to reserved SKUs.

maria: I dug in a bit — infra-bot: billing-scan job produced mismatch report -> `sku_map_review/2026-03-17.csv`. Looks like our committed reservations were tagged under different project IDs for a short window when a migration ran, so cloud didn't apply the discount to traffic routed via the new project.

infra-bot: Action: Created ticket INFRA-BILL-482 with the CSV attached.

devon: oof. can we reassign or request retroactive credit?

liam: we should escalate to finance + cloud AM. They usually can grant a retroactive adjustment if we show mapping error.

maria: action items: 1) I'll finalize tokenized cushion model and share deterministic numbers for us-east/us-central/eu-west by EOD Friday. 2) devon — can you run a sim accounting for long-seq workloads (seq 2048) and embeddings mix? 3) liam — own outreach to finance/cloud AM about INFRA-BILL-482. 4)ashley — approve short-term commit bump if numbers look sane.

ashley: ack. tag me when the numbers are in. :thumbsup:

devon: will run sim, ETA tomorrow morning.

liam: pinged finance + cloud AM. noted INFRA-BILL-482.

maria: also small ops change: add reservation tagging check in the migration playbook (quick check: `gcloud compute reservations describe $RES --format=json | jq .labels`). Prevents the project mis-tag gap.

ashley: nice. low lift.

maria: final note — if commit bump approved we can do canary increase for 48h in eu-west during predicted low-traffic window to validate cost vs fallback reduction.

devon: sounds good.

liam: thanks all.
